items.title: Apple’s buggy HomeView launch is making Google Home look good
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Early Apple HomeView buyers are returning their $299 smart displays due to buggy software, unreliable Siri AI, and setup failures. 
 Even prominent tech reviewers have criticized the experience, describing it as beta-like. 
 Apple has promised a December update to address some Siri AI shortcomings. 

Apple took its time entering the smart display market, giving Google years to establish itself in kitchens, bedrooms, and living rooms. But if the first few days of the Apple HomeView are any indication, Google may have less reason to worry about its new rival than we initially thought. Some early buyers are already packing up their $299 smart displays and sending them back to Apple.

The HomeView, which went on sale on November 13, has earned plenty of praise for its hardware . Unfortunately, the software meant to bring that hardware to life is proving to be its biggest weakness. Siri AI, whose delayed arrival reportedly held up the HomeView’s launch, is struggling with the very tasks that make a smart display worth having.
items.t: Apple’s buggy HomeView launch is making Google Home look good

However, it looks like Samsung may not limit these agentic AI features to mobile devices, but also extend them to smart home appliances.

items.title: Banana Native now runs 10 Switch 2 games on Android, including Mario Kart World
items.summary:
Credit: Oliver Cragg / Android Authority 

TL;DR 

Banana Native’s v0.3.40 update (and subsequent hotfixes) now lets you run 10 Nintendo Switch 2 games on Android, including Mario Kart World, Donkey Kong Bananza, and Pokémon Pokopia. 
 The updates also eliminate shader compilation wait times by compiling missing shaders in the background during gameplay, while also adding a Switch 2-style launcher, foldable screen support, and aspect ratio fixes. 
 Playing the native ports requires a legal game dump from your own console and a flagship Android phone with about 16GB of RAM. 

The Android emulation and native port scene is moving at breakneck speed, with Banana Native now running 10 Nintendo Switch 2 games on Android devices. Building on recent momentum around Switch 2 emulators and native ports on Android , the latest updates expand the project’s compatibility list to seven officially supported titles, including Mario Kart World, Donkey Kong Bananza, and Pokémon Pokopia, along with three experimental games.

Announced by developer moceure alongside the v0.3.40 release (and followed quickly by v0.3.41 and v0.3.42 hotfixes), the update also eliminates one of the biggest bottlenecks in running modern console ports on mobile: waiting for shader compilation. You can now launch a game before the preparation phase finishes translating every shader, with missing shaders compiling in the background as you play and saving for future sessions.
items.t: Banana Native now runs 10 Switch 2 games on Android, including Mario Kart World

items.title: Android Time Machine lets you try Android 2.1 through 7.1 right in your browser
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Android Time Machine is a website that simulates old versions of Android right in your browser. 
 It currently has eight releases, from Android 2.1 Eclair to Android 7.1.2 Nougat. 
 Each version runs on the Nexus phone it originally shipped on, and there’s nothing to install. 

Android is by far the most popular mobile operating system out there. However, the Android we see today is very different from what it was years ago, back when Google still named it after desserts (and not just codenames, either) and things like Material 3 Expressive weren’t even on the radar. If you’ve ever wondered what Android was like before gesture navigation, expandable notifications, or even an on-screen back button, a new website could scratch that itch.

Android Time Machine (spotted via 9to5Google ) is a web-based project that lets you run old versions of Android in your browser. The site, built by developer szabolevi98, currently offers eight Android releases, starting with Android 2.1 Eclair on the Nexus One and going all the way to Android 7.1.2 Nougat on the Nexus 6P.
items.t: Android Time Machine lets you try Android 2.1 through 7.1 right in your browser

items.title: I tested Pixel 10 Extreme Charging, but there’s nothing extreme about it
items.summary:
Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority 

Google’s November Pixel Drop is here , packed full of new AI, customization, and other features to upgrade your Pixel experience. The update also brings Extreme Charging Mode, fresh from the latest Pixel 11 series, to last year’s Pixel 10 range. If you’re not familiar with it, Extreme Charging aims to speed up your Pixel’s charging by pausing some background tasks, creating a little more breathing room for charging power and heat.

I wasn’t too impressed when Extreme Charging debuted on the Pixel 11 series . Even before using it, the feature was arbitrarily disabled until I’d charged the phone a couple of times. Once finally enabled, Extreme Charging traded higher temperatures for shaving about five minutes off the phone’s total charge time; a controversial trade-off in my book.

items.title: Google adds file attachments and sharing to Gemini Skills as Gems retire starting today
items.summary:
Credit: Adamya Sharma / Android Authority 

TL;DR 

Google has begun retiring Gemini Gems for personal accounts today, making existing Gems read-only before removing them completely on December 17, 2026. 
 To ease the transition to Gemini Skills, Google has added real-time file attachments (up to 100MB from Google Drive, Gemini Notebook, Google Photos, or local devices) and web-based View/Edit sharing permissions. 
 While instructions and supported files convert into draft Skills automatically, Skills drop support for Canvas, Deep Research, Guided Learning, and file formats like GitHub, audio, video, archives, and legacy Office docs. 

Google has begun retiring Gemini Gems for personal accounts today, shifting users over to Gemini Skills . To ease the transition and close two of the biggest feature gaps between the two tools, Google is upgrading Skills with file attachments and sharing capabilities.

According to a Google Workspace Updates blog post , you can now attach files from Google Drive, Gemini Notebook, Google Photos, or your device when creating or uploading a skill. Gemini references those files whenever the skill runs in a chat or task, and files pulled from Drive or Notebook update in real time, so your skill always uses the latest version.
items.t: Google adds file attachments and sharing to Gemini Skills as Gems retire starting today

items.title: Wear OS watches can now use your phone’s GPS to save battery life
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Google has released v26.45 of Google Play Services. 
 It lets your Wear OS watch use your phone’s GNSS to track location during outdoor workouts, which helps conserve watch battery life. 
 The Play Store v54.1 also adds the Pixel virtual gamepad for compatible games when your Pixel Fold is open. 

If you often use your Wear OS smartwatch to track outdoor workouts, you may be aware of the impact it can have on battery life. Google is now rolling out a new feature that should help.

Google has released a new version of Google Play Services (v26.45) that adds a feature letting your watch use your phone’s Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) to track your location during outdoor workouts. GNSS is a term for satellite-based positioning systems, such as GPS, Galileo, GLONASS, and NavIC. Running the watch’s GNSS receiver for an entire workout uses a lot of battery. By offloading that job to your smartphone, Google wants to make your watch’s battery last longer. Fitbit already offers something similar on some of its trackers with its Dynamic GPS feature.
items.t: Wear OS watches can now use your phone’s GPS to save battery life

items.title: Leak suggests Samsung delayed Quick Share’s Tap to Share for One UI 9.5

 Google debuted the feature on the Pixel 11 in August and promised it would “expand soon” to Galaxy Z8 foldables, but the feature hasn’t arrived on any Galaxy phone. 

Google rolled out Quick Share’s Tap to Share feature with the Pixel 11 series in August, promising it would expand to Samsung’s latest Galaxy Z8 foldables “soon” and to other Android phones by the end of the year. However, the feature has yet to land on Galaxy devices in any meaningful capacity, and new findings suggest Samsung is holding it back for One UI 9.5.

According to posts from the Telegram channel The Cipher Project , the “Tap to share” toggle within Quick Share surfaces with the latest version of Quick Share and its companion Connectivity apps only when the device is spoofed as running One UI 9.5. With the feature still missing months after Google’s announcement, this new finding suggests Samsung may have postponed Tap to Share’s rollout until the One UI 9.5 release.

items.title: US cities have some of the world’s weakest indoor mobile signals, Ookla finds
items.summary:
TL;DR 

A new Ookla study ranks North America among the worst-performing regions globally for indoor 4G signal strength. 
 Weak indoor signals affect 41% of measured buildings in Miami, 38% in Los Angeles, and 25% in New York, compared to just 2% in Seoul. 
 Weak outdoor coverage explains about 85% of the differences in indoor signal strength between cities, although dedicated in-building cellular equipment can significantly improve reception. 

Much has been made of the strides US carriers have made in improving their networks, with recent reports highlighting everything from faster download speeds to wider 5G coverage . But those improvements may not mean much when you’re struggling to upload a photo from your living room. New research suggests American cities have some catching up to do when it comes to delivering reliable mobile coverage inside buildings.

A new report from Ookla analyzed a year’s worth of mobile signal measurements across more than 100 cities in 60 countries. North America ranked alongside Oceania at the bottom for indoor 4G signal strength, trailing not only East Asia and the Middle East but also Africa and Latin America.
items.t: US cities have some of the world’s weakest indoor mobile signals, Ookla finds

A massive 7,000mAh battery is one of the biggest selling points of the Motorola Signature 27 , a phone that packs just about everything you’d expect from a modern Android flagship. But as we discovered last week, not everyone buying Motorola’s latest premium smartphone will get to enjoy that headline-grabbing battery capacity . We now know where and why.

items.title: Oppo Reno17 and Reno17 Pro are now official and they're quite familiar
items.summary:
Oppo has just made the Reno17 and Reno17 Pro official in China, following plenty of leaks and teasers. They succeed the Chinese Reno16 and Reno16 Pro, but with a twist - last year, the vanilla model was the compact one, with a 6.32-inch screen, while the Pro had a 6.78-inch display. This time around, it's the Pro that's small, while the Reno17 gets a 6.56-inch panel.

Both are IP69K rated, have metal frames and optical under-display fingerprint readers, and run ColorOS 17 out of the box. If their spec sheets seem eerily familiar, that's because they're very close to the Reno16 and Reno16...

items.title: Oppo Watch 5 debuts with 1.85" AMOLED, 7-day battery life
items.summary:
The Oppo Watch 5 was announced in China today, and it slots in as the latest fitness-oriented watch from the brand. It’s also the first Oppo smartwatch in a long while to feature a rectangular screen.

You get a 1.85" AMOLED with 390×450 px resolution and a 60Hz refresh rate. The display is rated at 600 nits global brightness and 1500 nits peak. It features Gorilla Glass 5 protection and an aluminum midframe. Watch 5 measures 9.2mm at its thickest point and weighs just 25 grams without the strap.

items.title: Gaming performance evolution: iPhone 15 Pro to iPhone 18 Pro
items.summary:
The iPhone has always had a great selection of games, including some AAA titles from older console generations. However, it was with the launch of the iPhone 15 Pro that Apple opened the gates for current-generation games to be ported over to the mobile platform for the first time. Such was the graphical leap of the Apple A17 Pro that, for the first time, we had the latest Resident Evil and Assassin’s Creed titles being available on a pocketable device.
